sections.title: Open with intent; release at the right boundary
sections.body:
- `os.Open` is read-only. `os.Create` is read-write, creates when missing, and truncates existing content. `os.OpenFile` exposes flags explicitly.
- The permission argument applies only when the call creates a file and is filtered by the process umask.
- Arrange Close after a successful open. In long loops, use a helper so each defer runs per item.
- For output, check Write, bufio Flush, optional Sync, and Close according to the required durability boundary.

sections.title: Choose the data shape
sections.body:
- `os.ReadFile` and `os.WriteFile` are clear for small, bounded complete values.
- Scanner handles bounded tokens and must always be followed by `Err`. Its default maximum token buffer is 64 KiB; configure a justified larger bound before scanning or use Reader for incremental large records.
- `io.Copy` transfers uninterpreted streams with bounded working memory and returns nil on normal EOF. It does not close or flush endpoints.

sections.title: Never separate byte counts from errors
sections.body:
- A Reader may return `n > 0` with an error. Process `p[:n]` first, then handle EOF or failure.
- A Writer that accepts fewer than `len(p)` bytes must return a non-nil error; `io.ErrShortWrite` names a short count without one.
- Copy returns the written count and first error. Source `WriterTo` has priority over destination `ReaderFrom`.

sections.title: Keep external boundaries explicit
sections.body:
- Use `path/filepath` for operating-system paths and `path` for slash-separated logical paths. Cleaning is lexical, not authorisation.
- `filepath.IsLocal` proves lexical locality but not symlink containment; use current root-scoped os APIs for actual untrusted access.
- `LookupEnv` distinguishes missing from present-empty. Load and validate typed configuration once, and inject lookup values in parallel tests instead of mutating the process environment.
